title: Autoclave

references.label: General microbiology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)
Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: A pressure vessel that uses high-pressure saturated steam to sterilize media, glassware, and biological waste.
operatingPrinciple: Steam under pressure reaches temperatures well above the boiling point of water at atmospheric pressure, which is more effective at killing microorganisms (including endospores) in a given time than boiling water alone.
basicOperation: Load items according to the manufacturer's guidance, allowing steam penetration around and through the load.
Select a cycle/program appropriate to the load type (e.g. liquid vs. solid/wrapped goods often use different cycle settings).
Wait for pressure to return to zero before opening the door.
Remove the load using appropriate heat protection.
importantSettings: Cycle time, temperature, and pressure — set per the specific load type and volume, not a single universal value for every load.
Liquid vs. dry/exhaust cycle selection, which affects venting speed and is important for preventing boil-over of liquids.
calibration: Periodic validation using biological and/or chemical indicators (see the Sterilization Indicators concept entry) and, per facility SOP or applicable standard, temperature mapping/calibration checks.
maintenance: Regularly check and refill the water reservoir if applicable.
Follow the manufacturer's periodic maintenance schedule.

commonErrors.problem: Cycle fails to reach or hold target pressure/temperature
commonErrors.cause: Door seal issue, overloading, or insufficient water
commonErrors.fix: Inspect the seal, reduce load size, and check water level per manufacturer guidance

commonErrors.problem: Liquids boil over during the cycle
commonErrors.cause: Container overfilled, or exhaust/vent rate too fast for a liquid cycle
commonErrors.fix: Fill containers to the manufacturer-recommended maximum and use the liquid-specific cycle setting

safety: Never open the door before pressure returns to zero.
Use heat-resistant gloves and a face shield when removing a hot load.
Do not tightly seal liquid containers before autoclaving — allow venting as instructed.
